chapter_theme: The close of Nondi Siddhar's song, under the heading 'I destroyed ego: the true state': at Manonmani's seat the poet hears the bell-sound of nada and sees Siva's dance, knows the mantra and the circle of Om, names the imperishable thing, takes the title of jnani, and in a nishtai where 'he' and 'I' are gone and the body does not perish he sees every arising as imagination and breaks into song. The chapter's claim is that the true state is seen, not argued, and that whoever takes daylight for darkness has no eye to see it.
structure_note: Sound and dance at the goddess's seat (2318); mantra, Om and the Indra seat (2319); the imperishable thing and the way to moksha (2320 and 2321); the open void and those who cannot see it (2322); the guru Mular and the Vedas (2323); nishtai with the body preserved and the unsleeping eye (2324); all arising as imagination, and the song at Chidambaram (2325).

links.note: In 2301 the teacher's dance is seen in the light at the nose-tip, silently; 2318 moves the vision to the goddess Manonmani's seat and adds sound, the ringing of bells and the song of nada, before the dance is seen. Sight first, then sound and sight together.

Both say the open space is there to be seen and that the fault is in the seer: Tirumular's people do not open their eyes even when it dawns; Nondi asks whether those who take broad daylight for darkness have an eye of knowledge at all. In both the inner eye, not the light, is what is lacking.

2307 calls Nandisar 'my grandfather'; 2323 calls Tirumular 'our guru'. Together they claim the lineage Nandi, Tirumular, Nondi, so that the guru's saying quoted here is traced to the Tirumanthiram's author.

Pattinathar's heart puts away pride and fear and 'sleeps without sleeping' to gain happiness; Nondi, with 'he' and 'I' gone, stays in nishtai with an eye that does not sleep. The same wakeful absorption after the same ego-loss.

2315 is certain the body is a false unstable cage with no substance; 2324 keeps the fleshly body from perishing in nishtai and counts that among the attainments. The conflict stands if ஊனுடல் அழியாமல் claims the siddha's lasting body; if it means only that the body is kept through the trance, the two stanzas are about different moments.

2298 reports seeing the arising (உற்பனம்) of supreme consciousness as a gain; 2325 says every arising seen through the expansion of the one thing is empty imagination. The later stanza turns the earlier vision into something to be seen through.

2318.reading: At the seat of the Mother Manonmani, hearing the ringing tone of the bell and the song of nada, the poet at once saw the vision of Siva's holy dance.
2318.nuance: மணிச் சத்தத் தொனி கணகணன: the inner sounds that yogic tradition lists, bell among them, as the stages of nada; the dance seen is Siva's as in 2301, but now at the goddess's seat (பீடம்), which may be a centre in the body.

2319.reading: The poet knew the mantra, reached and firmly knew the circle of the Omkara, realised the Indra seat, and seeing what the state of silence is, his mind took on goodness.
2319.nuance: ஓங்கார வட்டம், the circle of Om, may be a drawn yantra or the round of the syllable's parts. இந்திர பீடம், the Indra seat, is unexplained: perhaps the seat of the senses (இந்திரியம்), perhaps a centre named for Indra as the east. எட்டி அறிந்தேன் is 'reached and knew', not 'knew the eight'.

2320.reading: Worshipping and saying 'this is the imperishable thing', the poet rejoiced within and gained the joy of knowledge; praising that the state of moksha comes to those who know it as the way, he drove off the demon nature.
2320.nuance: பேய்க்குணம், the demon or ghoul nature, is the base disposition; Pattinathar uses the same word of the heart. The stanza alone makes moksha conditional on knowing the way (வழியாய் உணர்ந்தவர்க்கு), which gives the whole report its teaching purpose.

2321.reading: The poet knew the end of the Veda and cooled his heart with the thing that shines everywhere; he reached the space of nada, and to the praise of the people of the four lands he got the name of jnani.
2321.nuance: ஞானி பேர் பெற்றேன் under a heading about destroying ego is either unselfconscious or a reminder that the name is the world's, not his. நாத வெளி pairs the sound of 2318 with the space of 2322.

2322.reading: Those who have come to know 'this itself is the open void, and we are it' do not think of anything else; for those who looked on broad daylight as darkness, is there an eye of knowledge with which to see?
2322.nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the cut-open or bare space, is the Siddhars' word for the state with nothing in it; யாம் இது, 'we are this', is the identity claim the Vedantic Siddhars make. The question in the second half is rhetorical: the fault is in the eye, not in the light.

2323.reading: 'மூல முதலி மொள்ளே', so our guru Mular said in days gone by; clearing the doubt that the four Vedas spoke at such length, bliss welled up and overflowed.
2323.nuance: The quoted words are cipher or corrupt: மூல முதலி may be 'the root, the first' and மொள்ளே a verb of drawing or scooping (மொள்ளு), so perhaps 'draw from the root, the first', as a saying of the guru; the reading leaves it untranslated. நமது குரு மூலர் claims Tirumular as the poet's guru, as 2307 claims Nandi as grandfather. சங்கை may be doubt or the conch; doubt fits தெளிந்து.

2324.reading: With 'he' and 'I' gone, never forgetting the guru's grace, the poet knew himself by himself; he stayed in nishtai, the fleshly body not perishing, in the state where the eye that reached it does not sleep.
2324.nuance: என்னை என்னால் அறிந்தேன், knowing oneself by oneself, repeats 2317. ஊனுடல் அழியாமல் is the siddha claim that the body is preserved in trance or beyond it; set against 2315's false cage, it shows the two Siddhar attitudes to the body side by side in one song. துயிலாத விழி is the open-eyed absorption, as tradition describes it.

2325.reading: Knowing by understanding that all the arisings seen through the expansion of one thing are empty imagination, the poet saw the dance at Chidambaram and broke into a song of bliss.
2325.nuance: ஒரு பொருள் விரிவாலே: the many are the one thing expanded, and so விழல் (straw, empty) and கற்பனை (imagination). The dance at Chidambaram closes the song where the dance at the nose-tip (2301) and at the goddess's seat (2318) began; whether Chidambaram here is the town or the inner hall the verse does not say.

source_issues: 2323: the quoted saying மூல முதலி மொள்ளே is cipher or corrupt and is left untranslated.
